reviewerOrPass: CP280 separately identified same-AI source-first final academic, mechanical and content pass
independenceMethod: After repair publication freshly retrieved underlying programme API, human guide, research-practical, modern-drug-development, pharmacological-modelling, machine-learning and biochemical-laboratory sources. Reopened actual group/credit structure, admission rules and module content, then actual current workbook profiles/descriptions, methods and term/prerequisite cells. Challenged programme comparability, selected courses, all external placements and finished reader content from underlying evidence rather than the author correction summary. Same AI as author, not an independent person or a different model; runtime model/effort unknown.
academicChallenges: The current ordinary Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences pathway has 16 first-year modules (60 EC), 15 second-year modules (60 EC), two final-year taught modules (14 EC), three parts of the research assignment (16 EC) and 30 EC of open study: 180 EC in 37 positions. Individual credits for all 36 compulsory modules match. Computational and selective Pharmacy packages remain choices within open study; retired modules and the research parent are not counted again. The programme and key module API responses are unchanged; the human guide is accessible. Other module admission text was checked: the required laboratory safety test belongs to Introduction BFW and precedes practical work; second-year organic chemistry, modelling and practical preparation draw on the preceding first-year curriculum. Advisory statistics/programming knowledge is not misrepresented as an additional formal credit requirement.

The research assignment lasts ten continuous weeks and normally starts in April, after the earlier final-year teaching. Entry requires first-year completion and passed second-year practical units; one outstanding practical may restrict placements. Students must complete the placement questionnaire and academic statement on time. A research article and an extensive research proposal are equally valid products. Practical work, written report and presentation must each pass at 6.0 or higher. The maximum two half-days for other teaching or a resit do not permit concurrent courses or practicals. No additional EC are awarded for an extension. Detailed institutional timetables are not invented.

All 61 exact-target interests were reconsidered: 16 generator-eligible, 29 supporting topics, eight illustrations and eight outcomes. Drug action, molecular disease mechanisms and experimental evaluation are defining parts of the target alongside chemistry, design and delivery. Actual UCR Pharmacology teaches PK–PD, metabolism, toxicity, drug targets and quantitative response exercises; Molecular Cell Biology includes a drug-mechanism paper and poster. These supply a material response to the target, supported by physiology, biochemistry, pathology, genetics and laboratory methods. The comparison does not rest on generic science coherence or claim full chemistry equivalence.

The quantitative alternative retains this biological drug-action core and makes a substantive shift toward optimisation, neural prediction, calculus and systems. It shares 20 courses with the first programme and differs by four courses / 30 EC in each direction. The target’s compulsory modelling and machine learning and its optional computational direction substantiate the interest. General UCR mathematical and computing applications are supporting methods, not promised pharmaceutical projects. The first alternative instead retains anatomical, immune and neural-system applications.

The medicinal-design and delivery candidate remains infeasible against actual active course content. Environmental Biogeochemistry provides aqueous, redox and speciation chemistry, geochemical modelling and laboratories. R3 provides leaching, metal recovery and remediation laboratories. Neither establishes the missing pharmaceutical organic/synthetic chemistry, medicinal design, drug analysis or formulation sequence. Consumer Product Design concerns customer needs and prototypes rather than molecular design. The recorded laboratory shortfall concerns those pharmaceutical disciplines; it does not deny all chemistry-related laboratory provision at UCR. Biochemistry and molecular laboratory training receive full consideration within their scope.

All 37 placements were challenged: 16 partial relationships and 21 meaningful blanks. Biochemical laboratory training shares DNA isolation, bacterial transformation and protein purification. Mathematical statistics shares probability and inference while differing from Leiden’s practical R preparation; the later experimental-statistics alignment shares multivariable and categorical models. Molecular, physiological, anatomical, immune, genetic, pathological and PK–PD relations have direct shared substance. Modern Drug Development includes a substantial assessed pharmacoepidemiology strand, justifying a partial Epidemiology alignment while leaving its clinical dossier, regulation and commercialisation unmatched in scope. Numerical methods alone do not establish applied population PK–PD simulation and dosage evaluation, so that alignment was removed. Dedicated additional ADME, toxicology, chemistry and specialist laboratories remain separate where no additional adequate UCR counterpart exists. Optional independent research stays outside the scheduled 24 courses and 180 EC, beside the thesis; completion of a UCR thesis is not promised.

The two actual schedules each have 24 unique courses, four per term, 180 EC and Year-1 PPD, with six and eight advanced courses respectively. Every formal prerequisite and actual term offering was checked. Quantitative optimisation and neural networks move to their planned spring 2029 offering; cell biology and evidence synthesis can occupy spring 2028 after their required gateways. Physiology and biochemistry precede Pharmacology. Mathematical and programming foundations precede advanced computation. Description-only courses receive their full supported contribution without invented details.

Every finished reader-facing label, concept, external component title, block title, selected explanation, note, audience reference, year/route/status limit and source link was reviewed through the established renderer mapping. All 28 selected cached course descriptions and current course names were read. Only explicit audience component/cell notes are selected; internal sourceNotes and module codes do not become fallback prose. The current advanced research course title is correct. The complete curriculum and major specialist gaps are clear. Unchanged shared description reviews were reused with verified provenance; programme contributions were assessed separately. This pass used no Shiny, browser, screenshots, live modals or app changes and grants no runtime or release approval.
scope: All six stages, two actual alternatives, 61 interests, 28 selected course descriptions, 37 external placements and 22 published input versions. Case-level content approval only; app/runtime validation and final release remain separately controlled.
